title: Microwave-controlled interactions and stripe formation of static-field-shielded polar molecules
authors: Tiziano Arnone Cardinale, Malte Schubert, Stephanie M. Reimann
abstract: We study polar molecules where short-range losses are suppressed by a shielding scheme involving a static electric field and an elliptically polarized microwave field. Using perturbation theory, we derive the effective interaction potential and validate it against coupled channel calculations. We identify a parameter regime where two-body losses are strongly suppressed and the extended mean-field description of dilute molecular Bose-Einstein condensates is justified. We calculate the collective excitations and show that intriguingly, supersolidity in quasi-two-dimensional confinement emerges as a stripe phase even at small values of microwave ellipticity.
summary: This theoretical study models polar molecules whose interactions are controlled by microwave fields and static electric fields. By deriving an effective interaction potential, the authors predict that the system can enter a supersolid stripe phase even with small microwave ellipticity. This work advances the understanding of quantum gas control and exotic phase realization in ultracold molecular systems.
main_problem: The study investigates microwave-controlled interactions and the resulting stripe phase formation in a system of polar molecules trapped in external fields.
main_result: The research demonstrates that even small microwave ellipticity can induce a supersolid stripe phase in a quasi-two-dimensional molecular Bose-Einstein condensate.
method: The study employs perturbation theory to derive effective interaction potentials, which are then used in the extended Gross-Pitaevskii equation (GPE) and analyzed via Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) equations.
model_or_system: The system consists of polar molecules subjected to a static electric field and an elliptically polarized microwave field. The interactions are modeled using derived effective potentials, leading to a mean-field description for the gas dynamics.
key_observables: Collective excitation spectrum, ground state density, total loss rate coefficient, and the formation of the stripe phase.
important_parameters: Static field strength (F), microwave ellipticity ($\xi$), detuning ($\Delta$), and Rabi frequency ($\Omega$).
main_assumptions: The effective interaction approach is validated against coupled-channel calculations, and the GPE approach assumes the applicability of mean-field theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the dependence of loss rates and scattering ratios on field parameters, and show the excitation spectrum of the condensate as a function of ellipticity, revealing the transition to a stripe phase.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by deriving the effective interaction potential via perturbation theory, analyzing the resulting loss mechanisms, and finally applying the effective interaction within the GPE framework to calculate and map out the excitation spectrum, revealing the stripe phase transition.
why_interesting: This work directly addresses the control of quantum many-body systems using tailored light fields, providing a mechanism to realize exotic phases like supersolids in molecular BECs, which is highly relevant to modern AMO research.
